title: Grateful Dead Live at William and Mary College Hall on 1973-09-11
lineage: aud>?>7" reel @ 3.75 ips, no nr technics rs-1506>hd-p2 24/96>cd wave>adobe audition 2.0>flac; transferred/seeded by Rob Berger

ai_review.summary: Muffled but listenable audience tape captures a relaxed 73‑74 show highlighted by an epic Weather Report Suite and diverse Jerry tones.
ai_review.review: The recording is an audience (AUD) capture that suffers from muffled highs and occasional drop‑outs – most notably the chopped Dew segment – yet remains acceptable for fans of pre‑'78 tapes. Musically the concert shines with a spectacular Weather Report Suite, inventive Jerry Garcia guitar work, strong Dark Star, and solid performances of China > Rider, Playin', and Let Me Sing Your Blues Away.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is praised with several standout moments, while recording quality is only fair due to muffling and tape cuts; the combined weighted assessment yields a solid above‑average rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Muffled overall sound, decent clarity for an audience tape, noticeable drop‑outs and the Dew track is split into brief fragments ending mid‑verse; horns are audible but not overpowering.

standout_songs: Let Me Sing Your Blues Away
show_quality.setlist_flow: A relaxed first set with solid jams and classic numbers, followed by a second set featuring rare horn‑enhanced Weather Report Suite and Let Me Sing, giving the concert a laid‑back yet engaging pacing.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Displays an impressive range of guitar tones described as a 'seminar on pleasant electric guitar,' offering melodic phrasing without overplaying.
band_member_comments.Phil: Provides solid, steady bass work; noted for leading Dark Star and mentioned as being grumpy with photographers.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's vocals on the new song are passable and the keyboards blend well with the horn section, adding fresh texture to the set.
